_doc: Ironworks of the Steam Age (docs/eras/lines-steam-hv.md, S1): the steam alloy smelter sinters purified iron ore with coke dust,
then the Steam Blast Furnace (gtceu:steam_blast_furnace, recipe type gtceu:steelmaking) runs two modes chosen by the input: the
sinter becomes pig iron, the pig iron becomes Bessemer steel. (The type has three input slots, so no programmed circuit.)
server_scripts/grindless/steam/blast_furnace.js makes one sinter recipe per row of `feeds`: 4 of `input` + 1 coke dust -> 4 sinter.
Only iron ores that GTM 7.5.3 smelts straight into iron (furnace recipes of their raw ore): the oxides and hydroxides of
the Steam Age veins (iron, magnetite, hematite, goethite, yellow limonite). Pyrite is a sulfide: it waits for the LV
sulfide roaster. `input` is the purified ore of the material; `vein` is the steam drill vein that drills it (informative).
Yield stays GT's: macerating a raw ore gives 2 crushed ores, and each purified ore ends as one steel (0.25 coke in the sinter
plus 0.75 in the furnace: 1 coke per steel, like the PBF).
